clue.text: Lines up a ship in port

parts.note: an ode is a poem, a set of lines of verse

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: Lines of verse are written while a ship waits in harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns A and SS to give SSA, which follows ODE.
explanation.definitionFit: Odessa is a major Black Sea harbour city in Ukraine.

clue.text: No one book could raise this feeling

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising the pieces means reading them from the bottom upwards

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one
a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: Not a single book could stir up this sentiment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could raise' turns NO + I + TOME, which reads upwards as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A feeling such as joy or anger is an affective state of mind.

clue.text: Definitely not many bones broken

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Not many bones were broken in the accident, thankfully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges the letters of MANY BONES.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an emphatic refusal, meaning not at all.

clue.text: Common sort of friend Dickens wrote about

definitions.text: sort of friend Dickens wrote about

explanation.surface: A familiar type of companion appears in a Dickens novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Shared or held in common is one sense; Our Mutual Friend is the title of Dickens's last completed novel.

clue.text: Address for delivery?

explanation.surface: Someone asks what address a parcel should go to.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal talk to an audience is one sense; a speaker's manner of utterance, their diction, is the other.

clue.text: Immersed, cooked and gently boiled

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters have been worked over and changed

explanation.surface: Food was dunked, cooked and bubbled away on the stove.
explanation.definitionFit: To cook just below a full boil is the kitchen sense intended.

clue.text: Course involving the translation of poems

indicators.note: translating turns a text into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A literature course that includes translating poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translation of' rearranges the letters of POEMS. Epsom Downs is an English horse-racing venue, home of the Derby.
explanation.definitionFit: A racecourse in Surrey is the sense of course here.

clue.text: The making of Haydn's oratorio

explanation.surface: The genesis of a famous Haydn choral work.
explanation.definitionFit: Bringing something into being is one sense; Haydn's oratorio of 1798 is titled The Creation.

clue.text: Rehearsal for a ventriloquist

parts.note: a trial practice reads as an outing for the doll a ventriloquist works with

explanation.surface: A ventriloquist practises before the show.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial practice before the real event, with the joke that a ventriloquist's puppet would make the outing.

clue.text: Mother's in the outhouse drunk!

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a shed is an outhouse in the garden
Ma is mother, so Ma's gives MAS

explanation.surface: Mum is hiding in the garden shed, plastered!
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for heavily intoxicated.

clue.text: Determined to fight

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to have a scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: Set to describes someone resolved to begin a task; a set-to is a brief scuffle.

clue.text: Results of changes at the farm

indicators.note: changes shows the letters are switched around into a new order

explanation.surface: Consequences of reorganising things on a farm.
explanation.definitionFit: Consequences following an event, especially an unpleasant one.

clue.text: Travel the smart way

explanation.surface: Going places with style.
explanation.definitionFit: To journey by aeroplane is one sense; fly as an adjective is British slang for sharp or knowing.

clue.text: A lovable disposition may be most important

indicators.note: a disposition is an arrangement, so the letters are set out anew

explanation.surface: A sweet temperament may matter more than anything.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means first and foremost, before everything else.

clue.text: Take on work

explanation.surface: A boss hires someone for a job.
explanation.definitionFit: To hire staff is one sense; to use or put to work is the other.

clue.text: People in serious offence

parts.note: mortals are human beings
taken as written

explanation.surface: Folk caught up in a grave crime.
explanation.definitionFit: In Catholic teaching a grave transgression that cuts off grace.

clue.text: A local tour

parts.note: local is British for a neighbourhood pub, so the tour visits several of them

explanation.surface: A sightseeing trip around the neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'local' is a British name for one's nearest pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A drinking expedition taking in one bar after another.

clue.text: A small whisky for severe cold

explanation.surface: A wee dram to fight off the chill.
explanation.definitionFit: A small measure of spirits is one sense; a sharp chill in the air is the other.

clue.text: Swirling mist hides the way forward

indicators.note: one piece hides another by wrapping it inside
swirling suggests movement, so the letters are churned around

parts.note: a mode is a way or manner of doing something

explanation.surface: Swirling fog obscures the path ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swirling' turns MIST into IMST, and 'hides' puts MODE inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Forward in the sense of bold or presumptuous, lacking modesty.

clue.text: Fuss made by a dog losing its tail

indicators.note: a tail is the end, so the final letter of the word dog is dropped

explanation.surface: A dog makes a commotion after its tail is docked.
explanation.definitionFit: Bother or commotion, as in much ado about nothing.

clue.text: Dim sun, when out, will hardly encourage it!

definitions.text: Dim sun, when out, will hardly encourage it!

indicators.note: out means the letters are disordered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Weak sunshine is not much incentive for going naked outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when out' rearranges DIM SUN, and the whole clue describes the answer: a dull day hardly tempts anyone to strip off.
explanation.definitionFit: Naturism is a pastime best enjoyed in sunshine, so a dim sun discourages it.

clue.text: Footnote one added to letter from Greece

parts.note: PS, postscript, is a note added at the foot of a letter
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A postscript added to a letter sent from Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: A character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Bony ran Gaul in style

indicators.note: in style means the letters are fashioned into a new shape

explanation.surface: A skinny figure ran through Gaul with panache.
explanation.definitionFit: Bony and angular both describe a lean, sharp-featured frame.

clue.text: Guard sent to breached line

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a breached line is broken, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A guard is dispatched to a broken defensive line.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier posted to keep watch.

clue.text: Company car

explanation.surface: A firm's vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A companion or attendant is one sense; the Ford Escort was a popular British car model.

clue.text: He is taken in by a girl-who fluttered them?

definitions.text: He is taken in by a girl-who fluttered them?

indicators.note: one piece is taken inside another, so the second wraps around the first

parts.note: lass is a word for a girl

explanation.surface: A man is charmed by a girl batting her eyelashes.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer: what a flirting girl flutters to take a man in.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyelashes are the hairs fluttered in flirtation.

clue.text: A harvest on new soil in ancient Greece

parts.note: a crop is a harvest

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Gathering a harvest on freshly turned soil in ancient Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortified citadel, found in ancient Greek cities such as Athens.

clue.text: Outstanding result of love taking wing

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
taken as written

explanation.surface: Love takes flight as a result.
explanation.definitionFit: Owing describes a debt still unpaid.

clue.text: Praises the upper house in speech

indicators.note: in speech means the word is spoken and heard

parts.note: the House of Lords is the upper chamber of the UK Parliament

explanation.surface: Peers are complimented during an address.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent, LORDS and LAUDS sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol or commend.

clue.text: It can be made to display china

definitions.text: It can be made to display china

indicators.note: made means the letters are fashioned into something new

explanation.surface: A piece of furniture can be built to show off porcelain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' rearranges IT CAN BE, and the whole clue describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass-fronted cupboard is where porcelain is displayed.

clue.text: Angry about dress getting wet

indicators.note: about means one word goes around another

parts.note: irate means angry
rig is an outfit, a way of dressing

explanation.surface: Someone gets cross when their outfit is soaked.
explanation.definitionFit: To water land by channels, making it wet.

clue.text: Escape of fifty during battle

indicators.note: during means the piece sits inside the battle

parts.note: a fight is a battle
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Fifty men flee in the middle of combat.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleeing from danger.
